text:
RECOMMENDATION: RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 60

The panel's composition alone proves little — it's context, not evidence. Many all-male panels pick the best candidate; some don't. Don't build your case on it.

Your real case is the qualification gap: a master's in educational leadership and five years actually doing the deputy job versus "courses" and classroom years. For a leadership post, that comparison is hard to explain innocently. Add the unanswered request for written reasons — in most jurisdictions an employer must give them, and silence tends to count against them.

So: send a written follow-up, cite the deadline, request the reasons and the stated assessment criteria. Mention the panel composition once, factually, as part of the picture. Then judge their answer.
